about.lead: A service for settling meeting times by sending a single URL.
about.note: Open slots come from your Google Calendar, so connect it first.
about.step1: You send the URL of a booking page. No account or login on their side.
about.step2: They pick a time from the open slots and enter a name and email.
about.step3: Once confirmed, the event lands in both calendars and both get an email.
about.title: What Kimaru is
after.lead: What happens automatically up to the end of the meeting.
after.step1: A confirmation email goes to both you and the other person.
after.step2: The event is added to both calendars, with the meeting URL.
after.step3: 22 minutes before the start, they get a reminder email.
after.step4: The day's meetings show under "Today" and in Schedule.
after.title: After a booking is confirmed
calendar.p1.lead: Once connected, times you are already busy drop out of the slots. You only do this once.
calendar.p1.step1: Go to Settings → External connections → Calendar connection.
calendar.p1.step3: Choose the account you use, and allow reading and creating events.
calendar.p1.step4: Return to Settings and check that it shows as connected.
calendar.p1.title: Connecting
calendar.p2.lead: How to switch the account you connected, and how to disconnect.
calendar.p2.note: After disconnecting, slots are no longer worked out automatically and no Meet URLs are issued.
calendar.p2.step1: To switch accounts, select "Reconnect with another account".
calendar.p2.title: Changing or removing
calendar.title: Connecting Google Calendar
change.lead: What happens when a confirmed booking changes.
change.note: The meeting URL is replaced with the one for the new event.
change.step1: They open the management link in their confirmation email.
change.step3: On a reschedule, the calendar event moves to the new time.
change.step4: You are notified of the change by email.
change.title: Cancellations and rescheduling
contacts-about.lead: A list of everyone who has booked, with their history in one place.
contacts-about.point1: People are added automatically when a booking is confirmed.
contacts-about.point2: Each person's page gathers past meetings, answers and notes.
contacts-about.point3: Notes and scores need Pro; adding by hand needs Premium.
contacts-about.title: What contact management is
contacts-use.lead: How to pick up a follow-up meeting from where the last one left off.
contacts-use.step1: Open Contacts in the header to see everyone who has booked.
contacts-use.step2: Narrow the list by sorting and filtering.
contacts-use.step3: Select a person to see past meetings, answers and notes.
contacts-use.step4: After a meeting, record a note and a score (Pro and above).
contacts-use.title: Using contact management
group.more.desc: The features used from the second meeting onward, and what each plan includes.
group.overview.desc: What the service does, and how booking pages — the core of it — work.
group.run: From sending the URL to the meeting
group.run.desc: What you do, and what happens automatically, between sending the URL and the end of the meeting.
group.setup.desc: What to configure after signing up. Once this section is done, you have a URL to send.
index.heading: Instructions by feature
index.lead: Each entry covers what a feature is, how to set it up, and what each field means. Choose an entry to see the details.
page-about.lead: The unit you send out as a URL. Create one per kind of meeting.
page-about.point1: Length, meeting type and hours are set per booking page.
page-about.point2: You can have 1 page on Free, 2 on Pro and 5 on Premium.
page-about.point3: The URL starts with /b/, and anyone who has it can book.
page-about.title: What a booking page is
page-create.p1.lead: Creating a page and getting its URL.
page-create.p1.step1: Go to Booking page settings → "+ Create a booking page".
page-create.p1.step2: Give it a title that says what the time is for.
page-create.p1.step3: Under Time settings, set the length, meeting type and range.
page-create.p1.step4: Under Hours, set the days and times you take bookings.
page-create.p1.step5: Save. The URL beginning with /b/ appears.
page-create.p1.title: Creating the page
page-create.p2.field1.desc: The heading on the other person's screen.
page-create.p2.field1.name: Page title
page-create.p2.field2.desc: The end of the public URL. Left blank, one is assigned.
page-create.p2.field2.name: Public URL (slug)
page-create.p2.field3.desc: Text shown on the booking screen.
page-create.p2.field3.name: Description
page-create.p2.field4.name: Status
page-create.p2.title: Basic fields
page-create.p3.field1.desc: How long one booking runs, from 15 to 120 minutes.
page-create.p3.field1.name: Length
page-create.p3.field2.desc: Google Meet, Zoom, in person, phone, a custom URL, or to be confirmed later.
page-create.p3.field2.name: Meeting type
page-create.p3.field3.desc: What to pass on when the type is in person, phone or custom URL.
page-create.p3.field3.name: Location, phone details or URL
page-create.p3.lead: How long one booking runs, and where you meet.
page-create.p3.title: The meeting
page-create.p4.lead: The days and times you take bookings.
page-create.p4.step1: Open the booking page and go to Hours.
page-create.p4.step2: Tick the days you take bookings and set a start and end time.
page-create.p4.step3: Unticked days are never offered. Save to finish.
page-create.p4.title: Your hours
page-create.p5.lead: Time held either side of a booking, for travel or preparation.
page-create.p5.note: With no buffer event title, the held time is not in your calendar and can be booked over.
page-create.p5.step1: Under Time settings, set the buffer before a booking.
page-create.p5.step2: Set the buffer after a booking.
page-create.p5.step3: Enter a buffer event title so the held time lands in your calendar.
page-create.p5.title: Buffers
page-create.p6.field1.desc: Up to 2 months on Free, up to 6 months on the paid plans.
page-create.p6.field1.name: How far ahead bookings are open
page-create.p6.field2.desc: Keeps last-minute bookings out by offering only later slots.
page-create.p6.field2.name: Earliest slot from now
page-create.p6.field3.desc: "Automatic" spaces slots by the length plus both buffers.
page-create.p6.field3.name: Slot interval
page-create.p6.lead: How far ahead bookings run, and how slots are spaced.
page-create.p6.title: Offering slots
page-create.p7.note: 2 questions on Free, 5 on Pro and Premium.
page-create.p7.step1: Open the page and go to Pre-meeting questions.
page-create.p7.step2: Select "+ Add a question" and write the question.
page-create.p7.step3: Choose the answer type. Choice answers need Pro.
page-create.p7.step4: Enter options one per line, then save.
page-create.p7.title: Pre-meeting questions
page-create.title: Creating a booking page
pause.lead: How to stop new bookings without deleting the booking page.
pause.note: Opening a paused URL shows a page-not-found screen. Confirmed bookings are not cancelled.
pause.step1: Open the booking page in Booking page settings.
pause.step2: Set the status to "Paused" and save.
pause.title: Pausing bookings for a while
pinpoint.p1.lead: A link with an expiry date offering only the times you picked.
pinpoint.p1.step1: Select "Create a pinpoint link" on the home screen.
pinpoint.p1.step2: Choose the page and pick the slots.
pinpoint.p1.step3: Set the expiry. 3 days on Free.
pinpoint.p1.step4: On Pro and above you can hold the slots in your calendar.
pinpoint.p1.step5: Send the link. They see only the slots you picked.
pinpoint.p1.title: How to use it
pinpoint.p2.lead: How many links can be active, and what to do with used ones.
pinpoint.p2.point1: 1 link with 3 slots on Free, 3 with 7 on Pro, 5 with 30 on Premium.
pinpoint.p2.point2: At the limit, disable a link you no longer need in the list.
pinpoint.p2.point3: A disabled link cannot be re-enabled, and any held events are deleted.
pinpoint.p2.title: Limits and disabling
pinpoint.title: Pinpoint scheduling
plan.p1.lead: Scheduling works end to end within this.
plan.p1.point2: Bookings up to 2 months ahead. 1 pinpoint link with 3 slots.
plan.p1.point3: Google Calendar connection and automatic Google Meet URLs.
plan.p1.point4: Confirmation email, 22-minute reminder, cancel and reschedule.
plan.p1.title: Free
plan.p2.lead: ¥980 a month. Records around the meeting, and higher limits.
plan.p2.point1: 2 booking pages, 5 questions including choice answers.
plan.p2.point2: Bookings up to 6 months ahead. 3 pinpoint links, 7 slots, slot holding.
plan.p2.point3: Meeting notes and impression scores, and the advanced profile.
plan.p2.point4: The fortune-based read on each person, and richer reminders.
plan.p2.title: Pro
plan.p3.lead: ¥4,800 a month, on top of everything in Pro.
plan.p3.note: The paid plans have no free trial; you are charged when you sign up.
plan.p3.point1: 5 booking pages. 5 pinpoint links with 30 slots.
plan.p3.point2: AI assist that drafts what to raise with each person.
plan.p3.point3: Adding people who have not booked, by hand.
plan.p3.title: Premium
plan.title: What each plan includes
profile.p1.lead: What people read before booking. One profile per account.
profile.p1.note: A headline, formatted introduction and links need Pro or above.
profile.p1.step2: Fill in the Basics, How you work and What you offer sections.
profile.p1.step3: Select Save. It becomes your public profile.
profile.p1.title: Setting it up
profile.p2.field1.desc: The name shown to people, and what you do.
profile.p2.field1.name: Display name, title and what you do
profile.p2.field2.desc: What people judge you on. Be specific.
profile.p2.field2.name: Your strengths
profile.p2.field3.desc: Logical, empathetic, high-energy, listener or side-by-side.
profile.p2.field3.name: How you talk and propose
profile.p2.field4.name: What you want to settle
profile.p2.title: The fields
profile.title: Setting up your profile
share.lead: How to get the URL of a booking page to the other person.
share.note: Anyone with the URL can book. To limit it, use pinpoint scheduling.
share.step1: Pick the page under "Share a booking page" at home.
share.step3: Put the URL in an email or a message and send it.
share.step4: They open it and pick a time.
share.title: Sending out the booking page
survey-answers.lead: Where the answers people gave at booking time are shown.
survey-answers.point1: Answers appear under Answers in the header, newest first.
survey-answers.point2: Reading one marks it as read, so you can follow the unread ones.
survey-answers.point3: Past answers are also collected on each person's page.
survey-answers.title: Reading the answers
zoom.p1.lead: Once connected, meeting URLs can be issued in your own name.
zoom.p1.step1: Go to Settings → External connections → Zoom connection.
zoom.p1.step2: Select "Connect Zoom" and sign in to Zoom.
zoom.p1.step3: Approve the permission to create meetings.
zoom.p1.step4: Return to Settings and check that it shows as connected.
zoom.p1.title: Connecting
zoom.p2.lead: How to have each booking issue a Zoom URL from your connected account.
zoom.p2.note: Without the connection, no URL is issued.
zoom.p2.step1: Use "Test connection" in Settings to confirm meetings can be issued.
zoom.p2.step2: In Booking page settings, set the meeting type to "Zoom".
zoom.p2.step3: Select "Save settings". Bookings from then on issue a URL.
zoom.p2.title: Issuing URLs for bookings
zoom.title: Connecting Zoom
